correctness.rationale: For prime powers the equality is \(p^{au}(a+1)^v=q^{bu}(b+1)^v\). Distinct bases force \(p^a\mid b+1\) and \(q^b\mid a+1\) when \(u\ge v\); multiplying contradicts \(p^a\ge a+1\) and \(q^b\ge b+1\) unless both bases are \(2\). Equal bases are strictly monotone in the exponent. The exact identity \(F_{t,3t}(2^6)=F_{t,3t}(7^3)=21952^t\) supplies a noninjective parameter ray outside the proved region.

value.rationale: Prime powers are a natural complementary domain to the squarefree integers in the focal restricted-injectivity problem. The theorem covers all exponents uniformly for every \(u\ge v\), while the infinite collision ray \(v=3u\) shows the parameter restriction has mathematical content.
